raw: {"need": "Competence", "secondary": {"name": "Belonging"}, "read": "Going quiet and doing the bare minimum is almost never laziness; it is usually a retreat to a floor they know they can hold. They have likely decided at some level that full effort followed by failure is worse than low effort followed by a shrug. The belonging angle is that disengagement can also be a way of becoming invisible, staying off the radar of comparison with peers who seem to be doing fine.", "pull": {"collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Back off, lower expectations, and wait for them to come around on their own, which signals that you have noticed they are struggling and have quietly given up on them too."}, "mentorMove": "Name what you see without making it an accusation, and make it clear the floor is not actually safe because you are not going to let them stay there. Hold the full standard while making it clear you are going to help them get there, not just watch.", "holdFirm": ["Full engagement is still the expectation, not the bare minimum.", "They do not get to disappear from your attention by going through the motions."], "stayFlexible": ["Where they start re-engaging, whether that is one small piece or something they actually care about.", "How openly they talk about what is going on versus what they show through their work."], "forceLevel": {"level": 2, "label": "Questions"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I have been watching you and I want you to know I see you in there. You have not checked out completely, which tells me something."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "But something has shifted and I would rather hear it from you than guess. What is the part that feels pointless right now, or too hard, or just not worth it?"}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "I am not asking so I can fix it for you or pretend the work goes away. I am asking because I want to find the crack where we can get you back into this for real, even if it is small at first."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to more than this because this is not your ceiling, it is just where you landed when something got heavy. I have seen enough to know the difference, and I am not letting you convince me this is all you have got."}], "longGame": "The habit you want to build in them over time is the one where struggle does not mean retreat. When they learn that hitting a wall is a signal to ask for traction rather than a reason to stop pushing, they carry that into every hard thing that comes after this."}
situation: Someone I am responsible for has gone quiet and is doing the bare minimum.
